title: Derived internal Hom adjunction for derived pullback and direct image
statement: Let g:T\to S be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with derived pullback Lg^* [def-pc-derived-pullback], derived direct image Rg_* [def-pc-derived-direct-image] on the derived categories of [def-pc-derived-category], counit \varepsilon:Lg^*Rg_*\to\mathrm{id} of the adjunction of [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general], and derived internal Hom R\mathcal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For K,L\in D(\mathcal O_S) let \gamma_{K,L}:R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_S}(K,L)\to Rg_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_T}(Lg^*K,Lg^*L) be the adjoint of the canonical map Lg^*R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\to R\mathcal Hom(Lg^*K,Lg^*L) (the map corresponding under the tensor-internal-Hom adjunction [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction] to the composite Lg^*R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg^*K\cong Lg^*(R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)\to Lg^*L of the isomorphism of [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-product] with Lg^* of evaluation, evaluation R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\to L being the map corresponding to the identity of R\mathcal Hom(K,L) under the same adjunction). Then for M\in D(\mathcal O_S) and E\in D(\mathcal O_T) the composite $$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_S}(M,Rg_*E)\xrightarrow{\gamma_{M,Rg_*E}}Rg_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_T}(Lg^*M,Lg^*Rg_*E)\xrightarrow{Rg_*R\mathcal Hom(Lg^*M,\varepsilon_E)}Rg_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_T}(Lg^*M,E)$$ is an isomorphism in D(\mathcal O_S), natural in M and E. Moreover, under the identifications H^0(S,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_S}(M,Rg_*E))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_S)}(M,Rg_*E) and H^0(S,Rg_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_T}(Lg^*M,E))=H^0(T,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_T}(Lg^*M,E))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_T)}(Lg^*M,E) of [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections, lem-pc-derived-sections-pushforward-comparison], the map it induces on H^0(S,-) is \varphi\mapsto\varepsilon_E\circ Lg^*\varphi.

proof.text: Obtain a,bS,bT,t,gamma,z,eS,eT with their naturality, evaluation mate and zeroth hypercohomology equations from the compatible construction lemma. No invertibility is assumed in that lemma.

Whisker gamma by id.op.prod R, then compose with R applied to internal Hom of the counit. This constructs a natural transformation c. The generic counit-mate lemma proves every component invertible. NatIso.ofComponents applied to asIso(c.app P) defines d, with its hom component definitionally the required composite. The sections equation is exactly the supplied construction equation.
